Title: Bersatu will be given chance to defend itself before PN takes action — Rafique
Article:
MELAKA: Bersatu leaders should remain patient and refrain from making assumptions about possible disciplinary action by Perikatan Nasional (PN) against the party after the Melaka election.
Parti Pejuang Tanah Air (Pejuang) information chief Muhammad Rafique Rashid Ali said Bersatu would be given an opportunity to explain its position and defend itself before any decision was made.
He said, as stated by PN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar, the coalition was gathering evidence related to allegations of misconduct before taking further action.
"Yesterday, Datuk Seri Samsuri made it clear that PN would take disciplinary action, but evidence must first be gathered because we do not want to punish anyone without proof.
"So, while the evidence is being gathered, Tun Faisal (Datuk Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz) and his fellow Bersatu members should be patient and not jump the gun.
"You will be given the opportunity to respond. We (PN) will give you the right to explain your side and defend yourself before making a decision.
"So, to Bersatu, wait until the letter arrives because we want to settle the Melaka state election first," he said.
He was speaking to reporters after a press conference announcing the manifesto offers of PN candidates for the Melaka election at the Melaka Pas State Liaison Office.
He was responding to a statement by Tun Faisal, who had urged Pas to prove that it had not violated the PN constitution or denied members their rights before proceeding with disciplinary action against Bersatu.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: BN, PN target 60 per cent voter support
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional are targeting 60 per cent voter support in the Melaka state election through cooperation between the two coalitions.
Umno Supreme Council member Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Maslan said the target was based on the percentage of votes secured by BN and PN respectively in the 15th General Election (GE15), at 29 per cent and 31 per cent.
He said although BN recorded its lowest level of support in GE15, combining the votes secured by both coalitions could give them an advantage in the state polls.
"In GE15, BN secured 29 per cent of the votes, PN 31 per cent, while Pakatan Harapan obtained 38 per cent.
"When BN and PN work together, we can combine the support, with 29 plus 31 equalling 60 per cent.
"Our hope is that 60 per cent will vote for us and give us victory. Those figures are not made up; they reflect the actual results," he said to reporters at the BN-PN Gelombang Biru programme.
Ahmad said cooperation between BN and PN campaign machinery needed to be strengthened through more joint programmes throughout the campaign period.
"I urge the machinery to organise more programmes with PN, particularly involving Umno division chiefs and Pas chiefs, as well as Umno branch chiefs and Pas branch leaders.
"Only when we are seen working together can the 29 plus 31 per cent become a reality," he said.
Meanwhile, he said a mega ceramah featuring top BN and PN leaders was scheduled to be held at the Melaka International Trade Centre on Thursday night.
The programme is expected to bring together supporters of both coalitions as part of efforts to strengthen their cooperation ahead of polling day.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Netanyahu again seeks unity government despite mandate denial
Article:
JERUSALEM:  Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called again Monday for a unity government that would keep him in power, a day after opposition rival Gadi Eisenkot was given a mandate to form a coalition.
"A unity government is, simply, a necessity," Netanyahu said in a video posted on social media that ignored President Isaac Herzog on Sunday formally giving Eisenkot the first chance at a government.
Eisenkot's opposition bloc received 48 out of 61 seats needed for a majority in Israel's parliament in October 27 elections. Netanyahu's bloc won 53 seats.
But Eisenkot received a majority of recommendations in parties' talks with Herzog. He could rely on Arab-majority parties, which won a record 19 seats after unprecedented voter turnout on anger over racism and marginalisation by Netanyahu's far-right government.
In his video, Netanyahu warned Israelis against what he described as the threat of including Arab-Israelis in a future government.
"You cannot form a government with Hamas supporters, a government that depends on Hamas supporters," Netanyahu said Monday, repeating an often-used scare tactic against Arab-Israeli parties, which he has also accused of election fraud despite a lack of evidence.
The parties deny the charges. Eisenkot faces resistance within the opposition to including Arab-Israeli parties, which could also vote to put him in power without joining the government, leaving it fragile.
Netanyahu said that a unity government around his Likud party should instead include all Zionist parties as well as ultra-Orthodox Jewish parties.
Avigdor Liberman, a right-wing critic of Netanyahu and leader of the smallest of the core opposition parties, has made clear he opposes any partnership with Israeli-Arabs, questioning their ideology and warning of the political cost.
Liberman has instead courted the ultra-Orthodox, despite his years of criticism of the community over its key demand that its young people remain exempt from mandatory military service.
Liberman met Monday with Eisenkot in a public show of unity.
"Both expressed full confidence in their ability to form a stable government for a full four-year term," Liberman's Yashar party said in a statement.
Eisenkot and Netanyahu have both offered a national-unity government with the rival party – but with each one insisting he would be in charge.
Eisenkot has publicly said that Netanyahu is dangerous and unfit to lead Israel, pointing to his failure to prevent the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack, his deep divisiveness and corruption charges that could land Netanyahu in prison if he were to lose power. — AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Eight missing, nine stranded in Sungai Pertak water surge
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Eight people remain missing after being swept away by strong currents, while nine others are stranded in three separate incidents following a water surge at Sungai Pertak in Kuala Kubu Baru this evening.
The incidents involved three separate groups.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the eight missing comprised one member of a group of Yemeni and locals, and seven members of a group of 11 locals.
"For the first group, one person was swept away and has yet to be found. Upstream, there were about 11 people.
"Of these, seven were in the water and were swept away by the currents," he told Bernama.
The nine stranded people comprised four who had yet to cross the river and another five from a separate group stranded on the opposite bank.
Ashrul Riezal said the department received a distress call about 5.55pm and arrived at the scene at 6.30pm.
"We also received a call from the Orang Asli, who had led the group. The search is still ongoing.
"We have set up an incident command post to monitor water conditions and the surrounding areas, and locate victims who may be stranded at various locations," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Umno will not let past disputes derail cooperation with Pas
Article:
MELAKA: Umno has no intention of revisiting past disagreements with Pas, choosing instead to focus on political cooperation and the people's well-being, Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said.
The Umno secretary-general said past differences and contentious issues should no longer stand in the way of efforts to build mutual understanding and strengthen the spirit of cooperation between the parties.
He said both parties had agreed to put the past behind them and focus on a bigger agenda, particularly the interests of the people and the future of the state and country.
"I don't think there is much of a problem because we have reached an agreement to let bygones be bygones.
"In our efforts to work together, we must move forward," he said after delivering a speech at the Blue Wave campaign ceramah for the Pantai Kundor state constituency in Tangga Batu here on Monday night.
Also present were Perikatan Nasional secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan, BN election director for the Pantai Kundor state constituency Datuk Noor Azman Hassan and BN candidate for the seat Datuk Tuminah Kadi.
On attempts by certain quarters to revive past issues and disputes, Asyraf said such moves were not surprising and had not affected the spirit of the party leadership or its machinery.
He said attempts to rekindle memories of past political rivalries were also meaningless, as all parties were now more convinced of the importance of the cooperation being forged.
"That is why we are not surprised by attempts by others to dredge up the past. Such things are normal, but what matters is that we can see the leaders and machinery of both parties (Umno and Pas) have not been affected in the slightest.
"Bringing up all those memories of the past serves no purpose because they (the machinery) can see and are convinced that we must move forward," he said.
He said the people's interests must take precedence over attempts to revive disputes that were no longer relevant to the current political landscape.
"Moving forward, the people want this cooperation to bring prosperity to the state and country as a whole," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PN members told to vote for BN candidates
Article:
TANGGA BATU: All Perikatan Nasional members have been instructed to vote for Barisan Nasional candidates in the Melaka election on Nov 14.
PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the directive was aimed at ensuring a strong victory for the two coalitions in the state election.
"This is nothing new for PN. During the Johor election, we instructed our members to vote for PN in seats we contested and support BN against Pakatan Harapan in seats we did not contest.
"In Negri Sembilan, it was clear that we were working with Umno under the coalition arrangement there. Naturally, our members were required to support BN in all seats we did not contest.
"So this is nothing new in Melaka. I am merely reiterating the instructions given previously," he said.
With only a few days left before the campaign ends, Takiyuddin said PN was confident of contributing several state seats to the coalition's electoral performance.
"We see no major obstacles to achieving victory," he said.
He was speaking after delivering a speech at the Blue Wave campaign ceramah for the Pantai Kundor state constituency in Tangga Batu here today.
Also present were Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki, BN election director for Pantai Kundor Datuk Noor Azman Hassan and BN candidate for the seat, Datuk Tuminah Kadi.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump casts doubt on US midterm results with new fraud claims
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump renewed baseless allegations of voter fraud on Monday, questioning the legitimacy of last week's midterm elections after Democrats swept both chambers of Congress in a crushing defeat for his Republican Party.
"Does anybody really believe that this 'Election' was honest. How could the Polls be so wrong???" Trump wrote on Truth Social, alleging without evidence that large early-voting "dumps" had made Republican victories impossible.
"It's all about the machines, which are far more important than the voter!" he added.
The accusations marked a sharp reversal from Trump's initial acceptance of the results. "I am absolutely willing to accept those results," he told The New York Times on election night.
The president has repeatedly made unfounded claims of election fraud, most notably following his defeat by Joe Biden in the 2020 presidential election.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kedah MB's 1979 speech on wartime refuge transcribed after 47 years
Article:
ALOR STAR: A speech by Kedah's fifth Menteri Besar, Datuk Seri Syed Nahar Syed Sheh Shahabuddin, delivered nearly 47 years ago, has been transcribed from an audio recording, shedding light on a little-known chapter of the state's history during the Japanese occupation.
The speech was delivered on Dec 14, 1979, at the commemorative stone-laying ceremony for Kampung Lindungan Raja in Sedim, Kulim.
It recounts historical events in Sedim during the Japanese occupation, including how the late Sultan Abdul Hamid was given refuge in the village.
The transcription was completed on Oct 25 by Malaysian Historical Society Kedah branch chairman Syamsyul Anuar Ismail, who retained every word as recorded in the original audio.
"The audio recording is still kept by the Malaysian Historical Society Kedah branch. The language used is the everyday spoken dialect of the Kedah community," he said.
Syamsyul, who is also a senior lecturer at Universiti Utara Malaysia (UUM), said the speech was historically significant as Syed Nahar recounted the origins of Kampung Lindungan Raja, which were closely linked to events when Japanese forces invaded Malaya in 1941.
The speech also recalled how the late Sultan Abdul Hamid was taken to Sedim for refuge after his journey to Penang was blocked by Tunku Abdul Rahman Putra Al-Haj and several companions.
"One of the interesting accounts in the speech was how Tunku Abdul Rahman and several of his companions stopped the late Sultan Abdul Hamid from travelling to Penang.
"At the time, the Sultan was travelling to seek refuge at the request of the British authorities following the advance of Japanese forces in Malaya," he said.
Syamsyul said that, according to the account, the Sultan was taken from Bumbung Lima to Kulim before being brought safely to Sedim on Dec 12, 1941.
"This event also reflects the loyalty of Sedim residents, who were willing to shelter the Sultan when Malaya was under threat from Japanese forces.
"Syed Nahar himself stated in the speech that he was still a young child and living in Sedim when the incident took place," he said.
Syamsyul said the transcription was important to preserve the recording's contents in written form and make them available as historical reference material, particularly on Kedah's history.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cruise ship pianist rescued after 9 hours at sea
Article:
LOS ANGELES: A pianist working on a cruise ship was rescued by two fishermen after drifting for nine hours in the Pacific Ocean about 30km off the coast of California, US media reported.
The circumstances under which the 37-year-old man fell overboard from the Ovation of the Seas, a Royal Caribbean ship bound for Mexico, are unknown, CBS News reported.
The man, whose identity was not released, was hospitalised and was not in a life-threatening condition, according to the US Coast Guard.
In the incident, which occurred on Friday, two fishermen — Grant Garrett and Sean Norton — were returning from marlin fishing near Santa Catalina Island, part of Los Angeles County, when they spotted the man in the open sea.
Garrett recounted the rescue to CBS, saying he called out: "That's a human being. Let's stop the boat."
"Grant and I each got an arm and lifted him up, and he was in total shock," Norton said. "The only thing he said to me was, 'Thank you. I thought I was going to die'."
The fishermen issued an emergency maritime call, and a group of Newport Beach lifeguards responded. They believe the man fell overboard at around 2.30am on Friday.
Norton suggested the pianist may have survived for so long because of the exceptionally mild ocean temperature due to the El Nino effect.
"A different year, no way he makes it," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Wealth of the nation belongs to the people, not politicians
Article:
MELAKA: The country's wealth should be used to improve the people's welfare, rather than to make elected representatives and political leaders wealthy, said Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
The Pakatan Harapan secretary-general, who is also home minister, said the primary responsibility of elected representatives was to resolve the people's problems, not use their positions to amass wealth.
"Our country is wealthy, but elected representatives should not be. They work for the people. When the country prospers, its wealth can be used to provide for and safeguard the welfare of all segments of society.
"That is why we elect our representatives," he said when speaking during a ceramah in Klebang here.
Also present was PH candidate for Klebang Farzana Hayani Mohd Nasir.
Saifuddin said the government's ability to manage the country's wealth effectively had enabled it to provide various forms of assistance to the people, including fishermen, small traders, rubber tappers, padi farmers and senior citizens.
He said government assistance, including the RM200 Early Schooling Assistance for school pupils and RM2,500 aid for Form Six students, reflected efforts to use national resources to ease families' financial burdens.
He said the unity government had also managed the people's cost of living, including by maintaining petrol prices at RM1.99 per litre through subsidies despite rising global crude oil prices.
"That is how the Madani government manages the country's expenditure. Just show your MyKad. Now, oil prices are high because the United States (US) has attacked Iran.
"Shipping routes are blocked. Oil prices are rising. Global crude oil prices are rising. But prices at petrol stations have not gone up. We can still buy petrol at RM1.99.
"Why have global oil prices increased while petrol station prices have remained unchanged? Because the MADANI government provides subsidies to keep pump prices low. That is how we look after the people's welfare," he said.
On another matter, Saifuddin said Farzana Hayani was capable of serving as an effective elected representative in Klebang, given her experience working at the Prime Minister's Office, which could help her channel residents' complaints to the relevant authorities.
"If she becomes the elected representative here, and, for example, residents say the street lighting is inadequate and more street lights or solar-powered lights are needed, she can easily write to the prime minister and convey their complaints.
"I am confident the prime minister would readily agree to the request and approve it," he said.
He also reminded the people not to be influenced by political campaigns that played on racial and religious sentiments, which could lead to divisions within society.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: What the US midterms mean for Malaysia and the region
Article:
THE midterms have shifted the balance of power in Washington, but whether they will alter American foreign policy is an open question. For Malaysia and its neighbours, that distinction carries real consequences.
Democrats have won control of both houses of Congress but we need to be mindful of cliched references about President Donald Trump being therefore "politically hamstrung" for his remaining two-year "lame duck" period.
At first blush, congressional control by the Democrats may constrain Trump at home but let us not forget he is still the president and one who wields significant veto powers. It offers little reason to expect a more predictable or accommodating US.
American policy is increasingly shaped by forces that do not always pull in the same direction. Some reflect Trump's personal instincts and negotiating style. Others command support across party lines and are likely to outlast his presidency. The rest of us will need to tell the two apart.
Undoubtedly, the scale of the Republican defeat was striking. Democrats made gains even in traditionally conservative states, a result of anger over living costs, the war with Iran and Trump's conduct in office. His devoted supporters could not sustain the broader coalition that returned him to the White House in 2024, and two years later enough voters were ready to punish his party.
The Democratic victory should nonetheless be kept in proportion. Divided government is hardly unusual in American history, and Trump governed with a Democratic House during the final two years of his first term without showing much deference to Congress.
The incoming Congress can investigate the administration, challenge spending decisions and obstruct legislation. Democratic control of the Senate will complicate presidential appointments. Trump, meanwhile, retains substantial executive powers and his veto. Democrats lack the numbers to override the latter or to secure his removal from office following impeachment. Nevertheless, War Secretary Peter Hegseth will most likely be thrown under the bus to appease the bloodthirsty group braying for his pound of flesh, metaphorically speaking.
Washington may become consumed by partisan confrontation, with little to show in substantive policy. For America's trading partners, whose interests rarely feature prominently in domestic political battles, that prospect offers scant comfort.
Trade illustrates the difficulty. Democrats have criticised Trump's tariffs for raising costs for American businesses and consumers, and some restrictions may now face closer scrutiny. Economic nationalism has also taken root in both major parties. Protecting domestic manufacturing, resisting Chinese competition and using trade to advance strategic goals all enjoy considerable bipartisan support.
For Malaysia, the more consequential question is how far American trade policy has become an instrument of strategic competition. Tariffs may change, but it would be naive to expect any pushback in the use of economic leverage against trading partners.
The stakes for advanced technology may be higher. Competition with China over semiconductors and artificial intelligence (AI)  commands broad support in Washington. Senator Chris Coons, who is expected to chair the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, has called for an investigation into alleged connections involving Chinese intelligence and leading figures in the American AI industry. This was on the cards even before the
Financial Times
expose of Nvidia's Jensen Huang affair with Alice Huang, allegedly a Chinese intelligence operative. If indeed a spy, that would be the oldest trick in the book. Congressional pressure on Trump over China could therefore intensify.
Malaysia is particularly exposed here. Its semiconductor industry and expanding data centre sector have made it an important participant in global technology supply chains, and they have also drawn American scrutiny over the possibility that restricted equipment could reach China through intermediaries.
A more assertive Congress could press for tighter export controls, closer checks on end users and stronger enforcement against suspected diversion. Access to advanced American technologies may depend increasingly on satisfying US regulatory and security requirements.
Malaysia has legitimate commercial interests with both the US and China, and protecting them will require credible enforcement, clear regulation and sustained engagement with both countries.
Relations between Washington and Beijing may grow more complicated for much the same reason. Trump has shown a willingness to negotiate directly with President Xi Jinping, at times pursuing arrangements that diverge from the wider American strategic consensus. After his domestic setback, he may have stronger incentives to secure deals offering economic relief or a visible diplomatic success.
An understanding between the two presidents would leave many underlying disputes unresolved. Congress could challenge concessions involving sensitive technologies or security commitments, and American regulators would retain considerable influence over implementation. Like the rest of us, Beijing must now deal with an administration whose priorities may differ from those of other powerful institutions in Washington.
For Southeast Asia, these competing pressures complicate an already difficult relationship with Washington. Vietnam and Thailand remain exposed to American trade restrictions through their manufacturing sectors. Singapore's weight in finance and advanced technology brings different sensitivities, and Indonesia's ambitions in critical minerals and industrial development may meet American objections. The Philippines must contend with questions about the reliability of American security commitments amid tensions over Taiwan and the South China Sea.
These differences make a common Asean response difficult. The region nonetheless shares an interest in strengthening its own economic foundations and reducing vulnerabilities that outside powers can exploit. Regional integration remains incomplete, and the growing use of economic restrictions for strategic purposes makes it more pressing.
The war with Iran adds another source of uncertainty. It contributed heavily to Trump's electoral difficulties by driving up energy prices and household costs. His administration now faces competing pressures to negotiate an end to the conflict or resume major military operations, and Congress may have limited ability to determine the outcome.
For Malaysia, the immediate concern is the effect on energy supplies, shipping and global demand. As an energy producer, Malaysia has some advantages, but higher freight costs and inflation would still burden businesses and households. A prolonged conflict would also weigh on the wider Asian economy.
The election also produced a milestone. Abdul El-Sayed's victory in Michigan, making him the first Muslim elected to the US Senate, is pivotal in its own right. The Islamophobic attacks directed against him during the campaign, though, were a troubling reminder of the prejudices that persist in American political life.
As for the congressional stance on Israel, any suggestion of a major shift is wishful thinking. While progressive factions are up in arms against Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer and House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries over their alignment with the American Israel Public Affairs Committee   having benefited from the financial largesse heaped on them, chances are they will continue to lead in Congress, on account of the deep institutional backing within the party.
Trump's defeat does not mean the forces that brought him to power have disappeared. His successors may keep much of his approach to trade, immigration and relations with China, and even a future Democratic president would face strong pressure to protect American industries and maintain technological advantages over strategic rivals.
For Malaysia, the practical implication is clear. We must deal with the US as it is. Washington remains an indispensable economic and diplomatic partner, but effective engagement means working with Congress, regulatory agencies and the wider political currents shaping American policy.
This also calls for greater investment in our own capabilities. A country that depends heavily on foreign technology, markets and investment cannot insulate itself from decisions made elsewhere. Sound institutions, regulatory credibility and a more competitive economy can give us greater room to manoeuvre.
The midterms are a setback for Trump and an affirmation of American democratic accountability. For Asia, the consequences are less clear. The balance of power in Washington has shifted, but the forces behind American economic nationalism and strategic competition with China have not gone away.
Datuk Prof Dr Mohd Faiz Abdullah is Executive Chairman of the Institute
of Strategic and International Studies, Malaysia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NST Leader: No more temporary fixes — Malaysia needs a drainage overhaul
Article:
THE seasons are unchanging; the hot, dry season is always followed by the wet season. What changes is the country's landscape: verdant lands where forests and crops coexist will increasingly give way to urbanisation as the pace of development quickens.
This means the natural landscape and its capacity to absorb rainfall will inexorably give way to paved and concreted cityscapes, where only adequate drainage systems can spare us from inevitable floods during the rainy season or even the occasional heavy thunderstorm.
Thus, it is high time the country stopped treating floods as a seasonal emergency requiring temporary fixes and instead focused on the structural and environmental factors that make flooding a recurring problem year in, year out.
Social activist Tan Sri Lee Lam Thye has a point when he says Malaysia must move beyond repeated drain-clearing exercises and adopt a long-term flood mitigation strategy.
The country's ageing drainage infrastructure, as well as woefully inadequate drainage systems in most towns and cities, needs an overall review.
What is clearly needed is a comprehensive overhaul to address ageing or inadequate drainage systems, not another round of maintenance and superficial servicing whenever the monsoon approaches.
The National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) has previously outlined strategies and preparedness measures ahead of the monsoon season.
However, these are largely aimed at managing the consequences of floods as they occur rather than preventing them in the first place. Preparedness is important and necessary, for sure. But it cannot substitute for longer-term solutions.
Those tasked with flood control must resist the reflexive urge to repeat the cycle of reactive responses. Clearing drains and desilting waterways are routine and necessary maintenance exercises. They should, however, be only part of a sustained programme, not the be-all and end-all of the response to flooding.
Systemic weaknesses in the drainage network must be identified and addressed. A serious study is needed to ascertain whether our ageing infrastructure is adequate to address flooding.
This must include a comprehensive assessment of drainage systems, particularly in urban and flood-prone areas. Drainage capacity must keep pace with population growth, urbanisation and increasingly frequent episodes of intense rainfall.
Uncontrolled development, poor land-use planning, the loss of natural water catchment areas, inadequate retention ponds and deforestation all contribute to the problem and must be addressed holistically, not piecemeal.
There must be better coordination across the board, from the federal level down to state and local levels, with clear delineation of responsibilities, implementation timelines and adequate funding for approved mitigation projects.
The end goal must be clear to all: invest in flood prevention, not just recovery efforts. The economic and social costs of repeated flooding — damage to homes, businesses, infrastructure and livelihoods — make a strong case for sustained investment in flood prevention, which will reduce and ultimately eliminate the recurring need for flood recovery efforts.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Google unveils new AI chip variants as cloud demand surges
Article:
BENGALURU: Alphabet's Google introduced two new variations of its in-house tensor processing units (TPUs) on Monday, stepping up its challenge to Nvidia's dominance in the booming artificial intelligence chip market.
Alphabet shares were up more than 3 per cent in early trading.
Google's TPUs have primarily been used internally for products such as Search, YouTube and Gemini, but the company has been making the chips available through its cloud business to attract enterprise AI customers.
TPU sales made a meaningful contribution to results in the September quarter, according to Alphabet, with Google Cloud revenue more than doubling to US$30.71 billion.
The new chips, 8tx and 8i Max, are redesigned versions of existing processors tailored to specific customer needs, according to the company. Bloomberg News first reported the development earlier in the day.
The 8tx is aimed at government agencies and companies in regulated industries that need to keep sensitive data protected while it is being processed.
It pairs Google's chip technology with AMD's processors and encrypts data at the hardware level, delivering up to twice the speed of the previous version with virtually no trade-off in performance, the company said.
The 8i Max, meanwhile, is designed for AI applications that need to process very large amounts of information at once.
It combines two chips into a single package to provide additional memory and computing power, the company said, making it well suited to coding assistants, mathematical reasoning and drug discovery tasks.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka Pas confident cooperation with Umno will last beyond three years
Article:
MELAKA: Melaka Pas has dismissed claims that its cooperation with Umno would not last beyond three years.
Its commissioner, Zulkifli Ismail, said the remarks came from those opposed to the unity efforts between the two major parties under Muafakat Melaka, an understanding between Perikatan Nasional and Barisan Nasional.
He said PN and BN were committed to sustaining the cooperation, which was intended to extend beyond electoral contests.
"That is the view of those who do not support this unity.
"As for those of us working to make this unity a reality, we are not doing it for just three years. We will ensure it lasts forever," he said at a press conference to announce the manifesto offers of PN candidates for the Melaka election here today.
Also present were Pas Melaka deputy commissioner I Bakri Jamaluddin and four PN candidates: Datuk Seri Michael Gan for the Ayer Keroh state seat, Dr Mohd Yadzil Yaakub (Bemban), Rafie Ahmad (Paya Rumput) and Ridzuan Sarif (Bukit Katil).
Zulkifli, who is also Jasin member of Parliament, was responding to remarks by Bersama leader Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli, who said history had shown that Umno and Pas had never been able to share power for more than three years.
Rafizi was reported to have made the remarks during a Trak Kancil ceramah in Pengkalan Batu last night, saying Umno was not formed to share power.
On the momentum of the Muafakat Melaka cooperation during the week-long campaign, Zulkifli described it as very encouraging.
"Alhamdulillah, after a week of campaigning and with polling day approaching, I see that our campaign machinery is working very well.
"Coordination between BN and PN is at its best. I am confident that over the next few days we will see efforts to ensure voter support for Muafakat Melaka reaches its highest level," he said.
Zulkifli said several programmes had also been lined up to garner support from voters throughout Melaka, including simultaneous Blue Wave programmes in all 28 state constituencies tonight.
"We will also hold a Munajat programme on Nov 12, followed by a grand finale ceramah that night. We hope all people in Melaka will attend," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Single mother appeals for missing teenage daughter to return home
Article:
KOTA BARU: A single mother is appealing for her 15-year-old daughter, who has been missing since Friday, to return home.
Nurul Aida Alias, 34, said she was worried because her second child of six, Wan Zulaikha Mohd Zafari, had left home without taking any identification documents.
She said she only realised her daughter was missing the following morning when she found her bedroom empty.
Nurul Aida said she had lodged a police report and hoped her daughter would be found safe soon.
"This is the third time she has gone missing. Previously, she left home in March and September before returning a few days later.
"Please come home, dear. It has been four days since you left and have not returned. I miss you so much.
"If you read or come across this message, please come home, dear. I am waiting for you. I miss you very much," she said when contacted.
Anyone with information on Wan Zulaikha's whereabouts is urged to contact the nearest police station or her family at 011-49696018.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Abu Dhabi talks must show if Russia 'genuinely prepared' to negotiate: German FM
Article:
PARIS: US-mediated talks this week in Abu Dhabi between Russia and Ukraine on ending the war sparked by Russia's invasion will show whether Moscow is truly ready to negotiate a settlement, German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said on Monday.
"This is the crucial question that must be made clear in the discussions over the coming days: Is Russia genuinely prepared to negotiate?" Wadephul said on the sidelines of the G7 foreign ministers' meeting in Paris, urging Moscow to "give up maximalist demands" and warning against any "negotiation show" in the UAE capital.
[[nid:1574250]]
Speaking after talks with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Wadephul said they "agreed that there is a chance to end Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine through negotiations".
But he added: "The prerequisite is that Russia finally abandons its maximalist demands."
Wadephul warned that, against a background of continued Russian attacks on Ukrainian civilian infrastructure, "we see no substantial contribution whatsoever towards negotiations gaining any serious momentum" from Moscow.
"If that were to happen, everyone would be prepared to engage in a very constructive manner," he added.
"But Russia has not shown any such willingness thus far, and that is our shared position."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PN has strong evidence for action against Bersatu, says Takiyuddin
Article:
MELAKA: Perikatan Nasional has strong evidence to justify its proposal to take disciplinary action against Bersatu, its secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said.
He said the proposed action also covered Bersatu's complaint to the Registrar of Societies (RoS), which resulted in PN's registration being cancelled before the matter was challenged in court.
Takiyuddin said PN would proceed with disciplinary action against Bersatu after the Melaka election.
"The fact is that it lodged a complaint with the RoS, resulting in PN's registration being cancelled. It was not merely suspended, but cancelled," he said after delivering a speech at the Gelombang Biru campaign ceramah for the Pantai Kundor state constituency in Tangga Batu here today.
Also present were Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki, BN election director for Pantai Kundor Datuk Noor Azman Hassan and BN candidate for the seat, Datuk Tuminah Kadi.
Takiyuddin, who is also Pas secretary-general, said the RoS decision to cancel PN's registration was later challenged in court as the action was considered disproportionate to the complaint lodged.
"But when we brought the matter before the court, the court could not accept the cancellation as an appropriate course of action.
"So it is clear that this was an action that fell outside the norms of an organisation, including a political organisation," he said.
PN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar was previously reported as saying that any proceedings or disciplinary action against Bersatu would only be decided after the Melaka election concludes on Nov 14.
He said PN had received several complaints from component parties over alleged misconduct and disciplinary breaches, which needed to be examined in accordance with the coalition's constitution.
In response, Bersatu information chief Datuk Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz challenged Pas leaders to prove that the party had not breached the PN constitution before taking disciplinary action against Bersatu.
Tun Faisal also questioned Pas's cooperation with Umno and BN in the Melaka election, including whether the negotiations had received the mandate of the PN Supreme Council.

Title: Saifuddin: Nana's energy, proactive approach can deliver for Klebang
Article:
KLEBANG: Age is no barrier to delivering results when backed by a sharp mind and the energy needed in frontline politics, said Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
Defending Pakatan Harapan's (PH) decision to field a young candidate in Klebang, the coalition's secretary-general said Farzana Hayani Mohd Nasir had the qualities needed to earn public trust and serve at grassroots level.
Saifuddin said Farzana, fondly known as Nana, had the focus and intellectual ability to address community concerns.
"Her mind is sharp and active. If elected here, she has both the dedication and the capability to serve as an effective elected representative for the people of Klebang," he said at a campaign rally here.
He said Farzana's background in public administration, including her experience serving in the Prime Minister's Office, gave her practical knowledge of government processes and the ability to expedite constituency needs, from solar street lighting to student welfare.
Farzana faces a four-cornered contest against Barisan Nasional incumbent Datuk Lim Ban Hong (MCA), Perikatan Nasional's Datuk Seri Mohamad Ali Mohamad (Bersatu) and Bersama's Young Jie Yu.
"Whether it is writing in for 15 new solar streetlamps because an area is too dark, securing laptop assistance for university students, or repairing amenities at mosques and houses of worship, that is the core job of an elected representative: to champion problems and resolve them swiftly," he said.
Saifuddin also said elections should serve as a platform for public service, not personal enrichment.
"The country should be wealthy, but elected representatives and ministers must not enter politics to enrich themselves.
"When the nation prospers, that wealth belongs to the people — protecting the welfare of fishermen, small traders, rubber tappers, the vulnerable, and school-goers," he said.
He also urged Klebang voters to reject divisive rhetoric and racial fearmongering, saying genuine progress should not come at the expense of communal harmony.
"Politics in Melaka must have no room for those who pit communities against each other," he said.

Title: Malaysia calls for connectivity beyond populated areas
Article:
DOHA: Malaysia has called for a broader approach to global digital connectivity that goes beyond populated areas to include key economic locations as reliable internet access becomes increasingly vital to economic growth and resilience.
This includes as ports, railway networks and highways.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Malaysia was exploring the Coverage of Economic Areas (CoEA) concept to complement the existing Coverage of Populated Areas (CoPA) approach, reflecting the need to ensure digital infrastructure supports economic activities and national development.
He said Malaysia hoped the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) would explore the concept with member states as an additional approach to assessing connectivity and advancing inclusive and sustainable digital development.
"Building on this progress, we are now looking at how we can go beyond CoPA and also cover key economic areas (CoEA).
"This means looking at places such as ports, railway networks and highways, where reliable connectivity is important for businesses, economic growth and resilience," he said when delivering Malaysia's policy statement at the 2026 ITU Plenipotentiary Conference.
He said Malaysia had made significant progress in expanding its digital infrastructure through the National Digital Network Plan (Jendela), particularly in underserved areas.
"As of September, internet coverage reached 99.75 per cent of populated areas nationwide, while 5G subscriptions stood at 31.3 million," he added.
However, Fahmi said expanding telecommunications infrastructure was only the first step towards meaningful digital transformation.
Equally important, he said, was ensuring that communities had the necessary digital skills and opportunities to benefit from improved connectivity.
"For Malaysia, connectivity is not merely about infrastructure. It is about creating opportunities, empowering communities and improving lives," he added.
Fahmi said Malaysia continued to strengthen digital inclusion through its 1,099 National Information Dissemination Centres (Nadi), which provide communities with digital skills training and entrepreneurship opportunities.
He said Nadi joined the ITU's Digital Transformation Centres network in April 2026, reinforcing the country's commitment to empowering communities through technology.
On online safety, Fahmi said meaningful connectivity must also be supported by a safe and trusted digital environment.
He said Malaysia's Online Safety Act, which came into effect in January 2026, strengthened platform accountability and protected internet users, particularly children, from online harms.
"Complementing this, our nationwide Internet Safety Campaign has reached over three million participants, promoting digital literacy and responsible online behaviour," he added.
Meanwhile, Fahmi reaffirmed Malaysia's commitment to international cooperation in advancing shared digital priorities, noting that the country had been an ITU member since 1958 and currently served on its Council.
He also sought continued support from fellow member states for Malaysia's candidature for re-election to the ITU Council for the 2027-2030 term.
"Let us work together to make sure everyone can benefit from a digital future that is connected, inclusive and safe," he said.
ITU PP-26, themed "Together for A Connected, Digital Future", brings together member states to discuss global telecommunications priorities and the future direction of digital development.
Fahmi is in Doha to lead the Malaysian delegation to ITU PP-26 from Nov 6-11, and is accompanied by Communications Ministry deputy secretary-general (telecommunications infrastructure) Mano Verabathran.
The Malaysian delegation also included representatives from the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), as well as representatives from telecommunications companies, including Telekom Malaysia, CelcomDigi, Maxis and U Mobile.
As a specialised agency of the United Nations for digital technologies, the ITU plays a key role in international telecommunications cooperation, radio spectrum coordination and efforts to bridge the global digital divide.

Title: Malaysia developing national plan for post-quantum cryptography – Fahmi
Article:
DOHA: Malaysia is developing a national plan to transition critical information infrastructure to post-quantum cryptography.
This is part of efforts to strengthen cybersecurity and prepare the country for emerging threats posed by quantum computing.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said he had instructed the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) to engage with the National Security Council (NSC), National Cyber Security Agency (Nacsa) and telecommunications operators to establish a shared research and development (R&D) testbed.
He said the initiative would allow stakeholders to jointly test solutions and accelerate the transition to quantum-resistant cryptography in a secure and coordinated manner.
"As quantum communications develop, governments and industry players must build trust and interoperability through common standards, equipment testing and a phased transition to quantum-resistant cryptography, without disrupting essential services.
"Malaysia is developing a national plan to move critical information infrastructure to post-quantum cryptography. I have asked MCMC to engage NSC, Nacsa and telecommunications operators on a shared R&D testbed.
"This would let us test solutions together, and accelerate the transition securely," he said when delivering Malaysia's policy statement at the 2026 International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Plenipotentiary Conference (PP-26).
Yesterday, Fahmi said he had asked MCMC to hold discussions with the NSC, Nacsa and telecommunications companies to explore potential collaboration, to facilitate a faster and more secure transition to quantum-resistant technologies in Malaysia.
Quantum migration refers to the process of upgrading existing digital security systems to adopt quantum-resistant encryption technologies, designed to protect data against potential threats from future quantum computers.
Fahmi is currently in Doha to lead the Malaysian delegation to ITU PP-26, which runs from Nov 6 to 11. He is accompanied by Communications Ministry deputy secretary-general (Telecommunications Infrastructure), Mano Verabathran.
The Malaysian delegation also includes representatives from the MCMC and telecommunications companies, including Telekom Malaysia, CelcomDigi, Maxis and U Mobile.
As a specialised agency of the United Nations responsible for digital technologies, the ITU plays a key role in international telecommunications cooperation, radio spectrum coordination and efforts to bridge the global digital divide.

Title: Three cousins killed by lightning had been inseparable since childhood
Article:
SEPANG: The close bond shared by three cousins who grew up together ended in tragedy when they died after they were believed to have been struck by lightning in Bandar Baru Salak Tinggi.
Their uncle, Haris Salleh Kurais, 42, said the three had been inseparable since growing up in their hometown in Semporna, Sabah, before settling and working here.
He said his nephews, Mohd Sahrif Marusin, 26, and Mohamad Ahzam Marusin, 16, were brothers, while Mohammad Safwan Aksan, 18, was their cousin.
"I was watching television about 4.30pm when I received a call saying my nephews had been electrocuted. Then someone else said they had been struck by lightning.
"I got ready and rushed to the hospital. I was shocked. I never imagined something like this could happen," he said when met at Sultan Idris Shah Hospital in Serdang.
Haris said the three had always been close and respected him as their uncle. He last met them about two days ago when the family gathered.
"They were very close. If one went somewhere, the other two would follow. For example, if one was repairing a motorcycle, the other two would join him because they enjoyed repairing other people's motorcycles.
"They were also repairing a car belonging to one of them when the incident happened. I never imagined this could happen," he said.
Haris said family members in Peninsular Malaysia and Sabah, including the victims' parents in their hometown, had been informed of the incident.
He said arrangements to transport the bodies back to Sabah would be made as soon as possible after the police completed the post-mortems.
Earlier, it was reported that
three men,
including two teenagers aged 16 and 18, died after they were believed to have been struck by lightning while taking shelter in Bandar Baru Salak Tinggi.
Sepang police chief Assistant Commissioner Norhizam Bahaman said the incident occurred at 3.34pm.
He said Sahrif worked as an aircraft cleaner at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), while his two younger cousins were unemployed.
Several videos showing the three bodies covered with batik cloth and lying beneath a tree had earlier gone viral on social media.
The incident gained attention after residents and passing motorists uploaded photographs and videos of the scene.

Title: China dismisses spying allegations linked to Nvidia CEO's affair
Article:
BEIJING: China's Foreign Ministry has rejected allegations of Chinese espionage linked to Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang's affair, dismissing them as fabricated and defamatory.
Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun made the remarks on Monday, German news agency dpa reported.
The chief executive of the US chipmaker recently admitted to having had an affair, prompting Nvidia to launch an investigation.
However, the company's board said it had no reason at present to believe that Nvidia's trade secrets or US national security had been compromised.
Several media outlets had earlier reported that Huang could have become a target of foreign espionage because he had been in a relationship with a woman whom US security circles suspect was recruited by Chinese intelligence.
China's state-run newspaper Global Times also dismissed the allegations, saying US media had inflated the matter into an espionage scandal based on a few photographs of a woman with "Asian features" and Nvidia's efforts to ease trade restrictions on China.
Nvidia is a major supplier of advanced artificial intelligence chips.

Title: MoH prepares 85 medical teams, 387 personnel for monsoon floods
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Health Ministry has prepared 85 emergency medical teams comprising 387 personnel to respond to possible flooding during the 2026/2027 northeast monsoon, with psychological support also being lined up for affected communities.
The ministry said these comprised 36 Rapid Assessment and Health Rapid Response Teams, 34 Medical Rapid Response Teams and 15 Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) teams, Bernama reported.
"The teams will be mobilised as required to conduct health risk assessments, provide medical services and emergency treatment, carry out surveillance and control of infectious diseases, as well as provide mental health and psychosocial support to flood victims," it said in a statement.
The ministry has also made available 128 vehicles to support personnel mobilisation and field operations, while flood-related medicine supplies at warehouses operated by concessionaire suppliers remain stable, with stocks estimated to last between one and three months.
Through the National Crisis Preparedness and Response Centre (CPRC), State Health Departments, District Health Offices and healthcare facilities nationwide, the ministry has also stepped up preparedness to ensure continued healthcare services, particularly in flood-prone areas.
The National CPRC has been in Alert Mode since Oct 27, with continuous monitoring of flood situations, healthcare facility preparedness and coordination of response measures with State Health Departments and relevant agencies.
The ministry said healthcare facilities at risk of flooding had also been identified, together with alternative facilities in the event of operational disruptions. Plans were also in place for the early transfer of high-risk patients, including pregnant women and those requiring haemodialysis.
The ministry said the risk of flooding could increase if prolonged rain coincided with high tides.
At relief centres, the ministry provides health assessments, infectious disease monitoring, environmental hygiene inspections, food and water safety checks, vector control, as well as mental health and psychosocial support.
These measures are aimed at reducing the risk of flood-related illnesses, including diarrhoea, food poisoning, leptospirosis and respiratory tract infections.
The ministry also advised the public to use clean and safe drinking water, consume properly cooked food and avoid food contaminated by floodwaters.
People were also advised to maintain personal and environmental hygiene, wash their hands frequently with clean water and soap, and avoid direct contact with potentially contaminated floodwaters.
"Those experiencing symptoms such as fever, diarrhoea, vomiting and muscle pain after exposure to floodwaters are advised to seek immediate medical examination and treatment at healthcare facilities," the ministry said.
The ministry also reminded patients with chronic illnesses, senior citizens, pregnant women and children to ensure continuity of treatment and adequate medication supplies in the event they need to move to relief centres.
Separately, 59 members of the Psychological Support Team (PST) from various agencies, including the Health and Education Ministries, will be deployed to relief centres in Kelantan to help flood victims cope with trauma and emotional stress throughout the monsoon season.
Bernama reported that Kelantan Welfare Department director Che Samsuzuki Che Noh said the team would also organise activities to ease victims' emotional distress while they were at the centres.
He said the department mobilised 400 officers and staff, 13 counselling officers and 327 volunteers to ensure the smooth operation of disaster management and aid distribution.
Che Samsuzuki also urged the public to register early through the MyIBJKM application to facilitate the process when they are relocated to relief centres.
He said the information that needs to be completed in the application includes details of the head of household, family members, place of residence, and children's schools to enable victim profiling to be done earlier.
"This information is important for facilitating data management and preventing the duplication of information.
"Once registration is completed, the relevant data will be channelled directly to the National Disaster Management Agency, thereby helping to expedite the provision of assistance, including the Bantuan Wang Ihsan," he said.
He added that early registration also helps expedite the BWI payment process, including after the PPS is closed.
So far, 79,455 heads of household, with a total of 135,616 family members, have been recorded in the system, while 69,101 heads of household have registered through the MyIBJKM application in its second year of implementation.
He also urged the district-level Welfare Departments to intensify the campaign for the application registration during disaster management simulations to avoid congestion and delays in the registration process during floods.

Title: Traffic slows on major highways as Deepavali holidaymakers return
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Traffic is moving slowly along several stretches of major highways tonight as holidaymakers begin their journey home following the end of the Deepavali break.
A Malaysian Highway Authority (MHA) spokesman said that as of 8pm, northbound traffic on the North-South Expressway (Plus) E1 was slow from Bidor to Tapah, Kuala Kangsar to Changkat Jering, Bukit Merah to Bandar Baharu, Jawi to Bandar Cassia, and Juru to Perai.
"For the E1 southbound, slow-moving traffic has been reported from Kepala Batas to the Hutan Kampung Toll Plaza, Gurun to Sungai Petani Selatan, Sungai Dua to Perai, Juru to Bukit Tambun, Jawi to Alor Pongsu, Gopeng to Slim River, and Behrang to Rawang," the spokesman told Bernama.
Meanwhile, on the Plus E2, northbound traffic was sluggish from Jasin to Ayer Keroh, Simpang Ampat to Senawang, Port Dickson to Seremban, Simpang Ampat to Pedas Linggi, Putra Mahkota to Bangi, and the Sungai Besi Toll Plaza towards the city centre.
"For E2 southbound, the affected stretches are from Seremban to Pedas Linggi, Pagoh to Machap, and Simpang Renggam to Senai Utara," the spokesman added.
Southbound traffic on the Johor Causeway is also slow from the Sultan Iskandar Customs, Immigration, and Quarantine (CIQ) Complex towards the Woodlands CIQ.
"On the northbound route of the North-South Expressway Central Link (Elite) E6, slow traffic was recorded from Gamuda Cove to Bandar Saujana Putra, while on the westbound Kuala Lumpur-Karak Expressway (KLK) E8, traffic is slow from Karak to Lentang, and Genting Sempah to the Gombak Toll Plaza," the spokesman said.
Highway users are advised to plan their journeys, stay focused while driving, and maintain a safe following distance from vehicles ahead.
"Motorists are also reminded to indicate before changing lanes and ensure they have sufficient balance in their debit cards, Touch 'n Go cards, or e-wallets before setting off.
"The latest traffic updates can be obtained through the LLM hotline at 1800-88-7752 from 7 am to 10 pm, as well as on LLM Info Trafik, TikTok (@llmtrafik), X (@llminfotrafik), and the Malaysian Highway Authority's Facebook page," the spokesman said.
Road users can also check real-time traffic conditions and live closed-circuit television (CCTV) feeds via the MHA website and the Tuju mobile application.

Title: 1,084 flood victims sheltering at relief centres in three states
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 1,084 flood victims were taking shelter at temporary relief centres in three states as of 8pm today.
A check of the Welfare Department's InfoBencana portal found that the victims were housed at 12 relief centres in Selangor, Perak and Sarawak.
Selangor recorded the highest number of evacuees, with 694 people from 190 families at seven relief centres across four districts — Kuala Selangor, Hulu Langat, Gombak and Sabak Bernam.
In Perak, 383 victims from 116 families were taking shelter in Larut, Matang and Selama, as well as Hilir Perak.
Sarawak recorded seven evacuees from one family at a relief centre in Miri.
Of the total, there were 359 adult women, 334 adult men, 206 boys, 164 girls, 16 male infants and five female infants.
The evacuees also included 52 elderly men and 52 elderly women, as well as 16 male and 10 female persons with disabilities.

Title: COP31: Malaysia proposes 20pc of urban climate funds go directly to communities
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has proposed that at least 20 per cent of multilateral urban climate financing be channelled directly to local authorities and communities in informal settlements to strengthen their capacity to adapt to climate change.
Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming, who is leading Malaysia's delegation to the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), proposed the establishment of a Direct-to-Community Urban Climate Facility to channel the funds through predictable block grants.
"This would empower local authorities and communities to implement practical climate adaptation measures at grassroots level, including building retrofits for improved cooling, stormwater management and climate-resilient infrastructure, while ensuring vulnerable communities are protected from the growing impacts of climate change," he said during a UN-Habitat session on housing and climate action in Antalya, Turkiye.
In a statement, Nga also said climate-resilient housing should be recognised as a fundamental human right and a public good.
Citing a UN-Habitat review which found that 69 per cent of national climate commitments addressed urban housing, he said the challenge was to translate those commitments into practical improvements for people in informal settlements and other vulnerable communities.
Nga said Malaysia's integrated approach to housing and local government allowed national climate adaptation targets to be put into practice through building regulations, energy efficiency measures, and urban planning guidelines across its 156 local authorities.
Meanwhile, at the launch of Rethink Food. Reduce Waste. - The #OneBillion Challenge, he called for greater public participation in waste management, citing Malaysia's Separation at Source initiative as an example of how households could put national policy into practice.
"Last year, Malaysian families and communities collectively set a national record by collecting more than 27,600 kilogrammes of used cooking oil in a single day, demonstrating how everyday household waste could be transformed into valuable resources, including sustainable aviation fuel and green energy, provided all parties work together," he said.
Nga also highlighted Malaysia's Circular Economy Blueprint 2025-2035 and pilot Zero Waste District initiatives in KLCC and Penang as part of efforts to strengthen waste management.
He also witnessed the launch of the Malaysia Pavilion at COP31, which was graced by the Sultan of Pahang Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah.
Taking place from Nov 9 to 20, COP31 brings together world leaders, ministers, senior government representatives, intergovernmental and multilateral organisations, civil society groups, climate adaptation practitioners, and youth champions to advance global cooperation on climate action.

Title: Melaka polls: Anwar appeals armed forces, police personnel to back PH
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pakatan Harapan chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has appealed to armed forces and police personnel voting early in the Melaka election tomorrow to place their trust in PH candidates.
In a Facebook post, the prime minister said the mandate entrusted to PH candidates would be upheld with commitment and determination to serve all Melaka residents.
"Tomorrow, our friends and families from the armed forces and police will fulfil their responsibilities as early voters in Melaka.
"With humility, I appeal for your trust by voting for Harapan candidates.
"Your votes will determine whether Melaka is led by those who stand firm in upholding the people's trust or those who are willing to turn a blind eye when that trust is betrayed. To Allah, we surrender," he added.
A total of 12,531 eligible early voters, comprising 9,769 military personnel and their spouses and 2,762 police personnel will cast their ballots across 31 gazetted early polling centres statewide tomorrow.
Overall, 687,697 electors are eligible to vote in the state election.
The Election Commission has set polling day for Nov 14.

Title: Pahang Sultan opens Malaysia Pavilion at COP31 in Turkiye
Article:
KUANTAN: The Sultan of Pahang, Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah, today officiated the opening of the Malaysia Pavilion at the 31st Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31) in Antalya, Turkiye.
Tengku Ampuan Pahang Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah was also in attendance.
The Pahang Sultanate said in a Facebook post that the event is part of Malaysia's participation in the international conference, hosted by Turkiye from Nov 9 to 20.
"Their Royal Highnesses' presence reflects their support for efforts to strengthen the environmental sustainability agenda, the preservation of natural treasures, and international cooperation to ensure sustainable development for current and future generations," the post read.
The COP31 conference gathers world leaders, government representatives, international organisations, and various stakeholders to strengthen global cooperation in tackling climate change and accelerate the implementation of existing climate action commitments.
According to the post, the Malaysia Pavilion serves as a platform to highlight the country's efforts in the climate change agenda, while providing a space to share experiences, exchange views, and foster cooperation with the international community.
Also on the COP31 agenda are efforts to strengthen the Global Zero Waste Alliance through voluntary cooperation among nations, international organisations, local authorities, the private sector, and civil society to expand sustainable waste management practices and the circular economy.

Title: Four students caught cheating using AI glasses at middle, high schools in South Korea
Article:
SEOUL: Four cases of cheating using artificial intelligence (AI) glasses have been reported at middle and high schools this year, South Korea's Education Ministry said on Monday, Yonhap News Agency reported.
According to data collected from all 5,679 middle and high schools nationwide between Oct 27 and last Tuesday, one middle school student and three high school students were caught using AI glasses during their midterm or final examinations.
The middle school and one high school are in Seoul, while the two other high schools are in North Jeolla Province and the southern island of Jeju.
Three of the four students were caught repeatedly touching their glasses, while the other was caught switching to AI glasses after the examination had begun. In the latter case, the invigilator had been keeping a close eye on the student following a tip-off from another student, officials said.
All four students received zero marks for the affected examinations in accordance with relevant regulations.
In addition, separate disciplinary measures were taken against the three high school students, including three days of special education, four hours of community service and a five-day suspension. The middle school student did not face any official disciplinary action but was asked to perform volunteer work on campus.
The Education Ministry said it planned to distribute educational materials to students detailing these cheating cases, along with guidelines for schools to prevent the misuse of AI glasses.
The ministry added that it would discuss further preventive measures with regional education offices and the Korea Institute for Curriculum and Evaluation (KICE).
The ministry earlier said those caught cheating in the annual college entrance examination using AI glasses would face criminal charges and be barred from taking the test for three years, up from the current one-year ban.

Title: Melaka polls: Paya Rumput Indian community wants better-paying jobs, temple assistance
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 9 — Competitively paid job opportunities and assistance for the upkeep of places of worship are among the key issues raised by the Indian community in the Paya Rumput state constituency, which they hope will receive attention from the candidates elected during the Melaka state election.
Mechanical engineer Sathesh Kumaar A/L Gunasegaran, 24, said graduate employability and competitive salaries were important benchmarks in determining who should be elected to serve the residents of Paya Rumput.
He said the state government and the incoming elected representative should formulate initiatives to narrow the salary gap in Melaka and bring it closer to the level offered in states such as Johor, in order to prevent the migration of local talent.
“Among the issues I can highlight for the younger generation is, first and foremost, the unemployment rate. Perhaps Melaka is not on par with states such as Johor in terms of how they have brought about changes in salaries and job opportunities.
“Besides that, I also hope candidates can introduce activities or programmes that benefit school students and help improve their education and living standards,” he told Bernama.
K Selvie a/p Kannon, 58, said the Indian community in the constituency appreciated federal government assistance such as the Rahmah Cash Contribution (STR), Rahmah Basic Contribution (SARA) and other forms of aid, but also hoped that the needs of places of worship would be addressed. — Bernama pic
Sharing similar views, electrical and electronic engineering graduate Kuhan, 24, who goes by a single name, said Gen Z youths like him faced difficulties entering the job market if existing industrial areas in Paya Rumput were not fully utilised.
“It’s really not easy to find a job. Even as a fresh graduate, I’m actually struggling to get one. But honestly, I feel that if we vote for the right party that can establish a proper foundation for our country, we as Gen Z can lead the country and have a better future with a stronger foundation,” he said.
Apart from employment and salary issues, the Indian community in Paya Rumput also hopes that the welfare of its religious institutions, particularly places of worship, will receive attention from the constituency’s incoming elected representative.

The mother of five hopes that the elected representative for Paya Rumput will help ease the financial burden of relocating a temple from its former site to a new site purchased by the community.
“This assistance is not for personal gain, but for the benefit of the younger generation and our grandchildren and future generations, so that they can worship in comfort and safety,” she said.
